answer: The tower keeper reads the gauge each time an engine takes water, and the reading is written against the engine's number. A vine engine that never stopped for water fails the gauge: the level must have dropped at the quill of the taking, and an engine that drank nothing shows a full tower. Faking a season of water readings means bribing the keeper, forging two hundred entries and paying 7,600, while the jetty gauge book is read at every boiler washout, so an engine whose water was never logged is stopped at the next tower.
